flagged.evidence: The definition tests charts only “with γ([a,b])⊂U”; it never requires a parameter neighborhood of each parameter value whose image lies in a chart. If no chart contains a tested subinterval’s entire image, the condition imposes no regularity there. It therefore does not establish the local chartwise absolute continuity and continuity used by the curve-calculus claims.

Proof 2.1 asserts, “On each compact parameter interval, a finite subdivision into chart patches exists by local absolute continuity.” The cited definition does not provide chart neighborhoods around every parameter value, so compactness cannot supply the finite chart cover or the claimed almost-everywhere chartwise differentiability for a general manifold-valued curve.

Proof 2.1 relies on the causal-curve calculus to make u∘γ locally absolutely continuous and apply the fundamental theorem of calculus on [a,b]. That calculus’s finite chart-cover step is not licensed by the current curve definition, which lacks the required chart-neighborhood condition. The composite and the resulting conclusions in (b)–(c) are therefore not established from the listed hypotheses.

The page says, “It contains twenty-one mathematical items: six definitions and fifteen proved conditional results within the stated models.” Two of those fifteen results, lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus and lem-gr-temporal-functions-and-time-functions, are not established: their proofs require the chart-neighborhood regularity omitted by the current causal-curve definition. The page’s later caveat about the curve-calculus gap is consistent with this defect, but does not make the opening count accurate.
